title: 'Blee Blop Blues' and concert versus dance music
summary: They talk of a fast show-stopper that works in concert halls but not for dancing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: But, some of this is what we talked about before where when you were playing for people dancing -- that whole thing. And, when you're playing for people in a concert hall it's something else. I mean, you know that thing that you played for -- I don't know whether you still play it, but I always hated it from the first --
- Which one?
"Blee Blop Blues".
"Blee Blop Blues". (laugh)
(laugh) I always hated that fast number thing, you know, because everything was rotten on it -- you know -- the tempo, and everything.
You know, I've been trying to remember that tune because I heard it the other day, and I wished I could think of the name, and you just brought it up.
Yeah, but you know --
Yeah, I know. It goes beep beep beep, beep beep beep, beep beep beep.
Yeah. But, you play it in a concert hall and you get a great reaction.
Yes.
But, if you were playing that for anybody to dance to.
No, no. It's not really a dance thing. Unless you're playing for the Lindy Hoppers.
No. I don't think they'd like it.
(laugh)

Yeah, but it isn't that it's fast, it's the whole nature combination of the thing.
